verses.1: The desert and the dry land shall rejoice; the wilderness and the steppe shall exult and blossom like the crocus.
verses.2: They shall flourish and exult, even the glory of the Lebanon is given to them, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They shall see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
verses.3: Strengthen the feeble hands, steady the trembling knees.
verses.4: Say to those with faint hearts: Be strong, do not fear. Here is your God, the coming vengeance will arrive, the reward of God will come, and He will save you.
verses.5: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unsealed.
verses.6: Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute shall sing for joy, for waters have broken out in the desert, and streams in the steppe.
verses.7: And the parched land will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. There the jackals will lie down, and the reeds and thickets will cover the place with lush grass.
verses.8: A highway shall be there, a road, and it shall be called the Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, nor shall fools travel it—it is for those who walk, and the foolish shall not stray.
verses.9: There will be no lion there, no ravenous beast shall ascend it. No predator will be found there; only the ransomed shall walk.
verses.10: The redeemed of the LORD shall return, coming to Zion with singing and joy on their heads. Joy and gladness shall pursue them, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 4: The phrase "Here is your God" follows the Hebrew "הִנֵּה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם" and is rendered as a direct address to the people.  
- v. 7: The reference to jackals (שָׁרָב) and reeds (קָנֶה וָגֹֽמֶא) is read contextually as describing the lushness of the restored land, not as literal wildlife.  
- v. 9: The plural "ransomed" (גְּאוּלִֽים) is rendered as "the ransomed" to reflect the collective deliverance.
